# ExtremeXOS (EXOS) — MIB Reference

## Standard MIBs supported

EXOS's own "SNMP MIBs User Guide" section confirms EXOS ships a "Supported Standards, Protocols, and MIBs" list split into RFC-standard and Extreme-proprietary sections, but the specific per-MIB support table did not render through automated fetch this session (the documentation page appears to require in-browser navigation/JS beyond a plain table of contents). Treat the following as **expected-present based on general EXOS/enterprise-switch convention and cross-references found in search results**, not confirmed line-by-line against Extreme's own list:

| Standard MIB | Expected support on EXOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **SNMPv2-MIB** (RFC 3418) | Yes | Baseline `system` group; used for device identification the same way as every other vendor (`sysObjectID` resolves under Extreme's PEN `1.3.6.1.4.1.1916`). |
| **IF-MIB** (RFC 2863) | Yes | `ifTable`/`ifXTable`, `ifAdminStatus`/`ifOperStatus`/`ifAlias` per the cross-vendor baseline in `standard-mibs.md`. |
| **BRIDGE-MIB** (RFC 4188) | Yes | Classic 802.1D bridging/STP read-side baseline; EXOS's STPD model (see `cli-reference.md`) is exposed here for legacy per-port STP state alongside/superseded-by richer info in Extreme's own STP-related enterprise MIB (see below, existence confirmed but object list not obtained this session). |
| **Q-BRIDGE-MIB** (RFC 4363) | Yes | VLAN membership. **Confirmed read-write** — see dedicated section below; this is a first-hand read of Extreme's own EXOS documentation, not a search-summary or third-party-mirror inference. |
| **LLDP-MIB** (IEEE 802.1AB) | Yes | Referenced widely in Extreme community/topology-discovery discussions; not directly re-confirmed via a primary EXOS doc page this session. |
| **ENTITY-MIB** (RFC 6933/4133) | Yes | Chassis/module/port physical inventory; expected present on modular/stackable EXOS platforms. |
| **RMON-MIB** (RFC 2819) | Yes | EXOS documentation elsewhere references RMON alarm/event configuration; not separately re-verified this session. |

**Action item for whoever next touches this file**: confirm the above against a live EXOS switch (`show version` plus a MIB-browser walk of `1.3.6.1.2.1.*`) or by successfully rendering `https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_30.1/GUID-F9C71D9A-4D53-47DB-B194-67ACB956BE37.shtml` in an actual browser, since the automated fetch in this session only returned the page's outer TOC structure.

## Q-BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4363) — VLAN write support, confirmed

**Resolved this session** (previous "not independently confirmed" flag lifted). A prior research pass found what looked like SNMP-write confirmation for Q-BRIDGE-MIB VLAN objects on an Extreme switch, but the page turned out to document the **ExtremeSwitching 200 Series — a different, non-EXOS product line** (correctly discarded, not applied). This pass re-ran the search scoped specifically to `documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_*` paths and got a first-hand, primary-source hit: Extreme's own **EXOS 30.6 User Guide**, "RFC 4363 (Q-BRIDGE-MIB)" page (`GUID-20EAEBB1-916D-4995-B71B-48100338AA82`), fetched directly (raw HTML, not a search-engine summary) and cross-checked against the same page's TOC entry under exos_22.5 to confirm the GUID is stable across versions.

Per-object access, quoted from that page:

| Object | Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dot1qPvid` | **Read-Write** | "The PVID, the VLAN-ID assigned to untagged frames or Priority-Tagged frames received on this port." — this is EXOS's access-VLAN/PVID SNMP-write path, directly analogous to the confirmed `dot1qPvid` write on Huawei and Aruba documented elsewhere in this docs tree. |
| `dot1qVlanStaticName` | Read-Create | Administratively assigned VLAN name string. |
| `dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts` | Read-Create | **Supported, but EXOS does not implement separate egress/ingress state** — writing this set makes the specified ports both egress *and* ingress members of the VLAN (a real EXOS-specific deviation from the RFC's separate egress/ingress model — worth flagging to any GUI action that assumes egress-only semantics). |
| `dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` | Read-Create | Same egress/ingress-conflation caveat as above — supported, but interpreted as untagged egress+ingress membership. |
| `dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus` | Read-Create | **VLAN creation/deletion is SNMP-writable, but with a restricted RowStatus subset**: only `createAndGo(4)` and `destroy(6)` are implemented; `createAndWait(5)` is accepted but behaves like `createAndGo(4)` (i.e. EXOS has no real two-phase create — this matters for a GUI/agent implementation that assumes standard RowStatus semantics across vendors). |
| `dot1qVlanForbiddenEgressPorts` | Not supported | SNMP GET always returns zeroes — do not attempt to write this object on EXOS. |
| `dot1qGvrpStatus` / `dot1qPortGvrpStatus` / `dot1qPortIngressFiltering` / `dot1qPortRestrictedVlanRegistration` | Read-write | GVRP and ingress-filtering controls, confirmed on the same page — not core to VLAN-membership write but noted since they're on the same table. |
| `dot1qVlanCurrentTable` (`dot1qVlanFdbId`, `dot1qVlanCurrentEgressPorts`, `dot1qVlanCurrentUntaggedPorts`, `dot1qVlanStatus`, `dot1qVlanCreationTime`) | Read-only | The "current" (as opposed to "static"/administratively-configured) VLAN state table — confirms this is a read-only mirror, not a second write path. |

**Bottom line for SignalScope**: EXOS has a genuine, EXOS-documented SNMP-write path for VLAN port membership (`dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts`/`dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts`), PVID/access-VLAN assignment (`dot1qPvid`), and VLAN creation/deletion (`dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus`, createAndGo/destroy only) — this moves EXOS from "plausible, unconfirmed" to confirmed for the same category of write Huawei and Aruba have. The write scope is narrower than Aruba's (no confirmed trunk-allowed-list-equivalent or STP-edge-port object found on this pass — only what's in Q-BRIDGE-MIB, no Extreme-proprietary MIB was checked for additional write objects this session) but broader than what was previously documented for EXOS. Source: [RFC 4363 (Q-BRIDGE-MIB) — ExtremeXOS User Guide, version 30.6](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_30.6/GUID-20EAEBB1-916D-4995-B71B-48100338AA82.shtml).

## Extreme enterprise MIBs

All rooted under Extreme's IANA private enterprise number **1916** (`1.3.6.1.4.1.1916`). OIDs below beyond the PEN root are sourced from a **third-party MIB-browser mirror** (`mibs.observium.org`), not fetched directly from an Extreme-hosted `.mib`/`.my` file this session — flagged explicitly per-row; treat numeric leaf OIDs as "likely correct, confirm against the vendored/downloaded MIB text or a live walk before depending on them for a production SNMP SET."

| MIB | Base OID | Confirmed via | Purpose | Notable objects (third-party-mirror sourced, unconfirmed against primary) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EXTREME-SYSTEM-MIB** | `1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.1.1` (`extremeSystem`) | Existence + doc-section placement confirmed via [Extreme's own doc page](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_30.5/GUID-7B2EA11E-6CE5-4822-8F22-511B7D4F8D70.shtml) | System-level identification, environmental (temperature) sensors, and **config-save control** | `extremeSaveConfiguration` (`.1.1.1.3`) — described by the mirror as a save-trigger object, the closest EXOS analog to Cisco's `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` "SNMP SET to trigger `write memory`-equivalent" pattern; `extremeSaveStatus` (`.1.1.1.4`); `extremeCurrentConfigInUse` (`.1.1.1.5`); `extremeConfigToUseOnReboot` (`.1.1.1.6`, i.e. which of `primary`/`secondary` boots next — the SNMP equivalent of CLI `use configuration`); `extremeCurrentTemperature` (`.1.1.1.8`); `extremeOverTemperatureAlarm` (`.1.1.1.7`); `extremeSystemID`/`extremeSystemBoardID` (`.1.1.1.16`/`.17`). **Not independently verified against Extreme's own MIB text this session** — treat leaf OIDs as provisional. |
| **EXTREME-VLAN-MIB** | `1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.1.2` (`extremeVlan`) | Existence confirmed via third-party mirror only | Extreme's own VLAN configuration surface, parallel to (not a replacement for) `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` | `extremeVlanIfTable` (`.2.1.2`) with `extremeVlanIfVlanId` (`.2.1.2.1.10`), `extremeVlanIfEncapsType` (`.2.1.2.1.11`, 802.1Q vs none), `extremeVlanIfStatus` (`.2.1.2.1.6`, RowStatus-style create/delete); `extremeVlanOpaqueTable` (`.2.6.1`) with `extremeVlanOpaqueTaggedPorts`/`extremeVlanOpaqueUntaggedPorts` (`.2.6.1.1.1`/`.1.2`) — a port-bitmask pair directly analogous to `Q-BRIDGE-MIB`'s `dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts`/`dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts`; `extremeVlanStackTable` (`.2.7.1`) for VLAN-stacking (Q-in-Q) relationships. **Not independently verified against Extreme's own MIB text this session.** |
| **EXTREME-SNMPv3-MIB** | `1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.1.23` (`extremeSnmpv3`) | Existence confirmed via [Extreme's own doc page listing](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_22.5/GUID-70F85543-2561-48B6-BA62-AE43D120CD1E.shtml) and third-party mirror | Extreme-specific extensions to the standard SNMPv3 (`SNMP-USER-BASED-SM-MIB`/`SNMP-VIEW-BASED-ACM-MIB`) framework — the CLI-level `configure snmpv3 add mib-view`/`add access`/`add group` commands document said to configure objects in this space, alongside the IETF-standard USM/VACM MIBs. Object-level detail not obtained this session — this MIB's practical content is that it supplements rather than replaces the standard SNMPv3 MIBs. |
| **EXTREME-STP-EXTENSIONS-MIB** (`extremeStp`) | `1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.1.17` | Existence + PEN sub-arc confirmed via third-party mirror search only | Extreme's STPD-aware extensions on top of `BRIDGE-MIB`'s classic 802.1D-only view — plausibly where per-STPD-domain state (vs. per-VLAN or per-bridge state) is exposed, given EXOS's STPD abstraction has no direct one-to-one standard-MIB equivalent. **Object list not obtained this session** — flagged here mainly to confirm the MIB exists and give a starting OID for a future deep-dive, not as a usable object reference yet. |

Note: Extreme's `EXTREME-BASE-MIB` (root arc definitions) and further per-feature MIBs (QoS, PoE, stacking, etc.) certainly exist under the same `1916` PEN — this file intentionally covers only the objects called out in this assignment's brief (system/save, VLAN, SNMPv3, STP) rather than attempting a full enterprise-MIB inventory.

## SNMPv3 `mib-view` access-control mechanism (distinctive — cross-reference Huawei)

EXOS's SNMPv3 write/read authorization model is built from four linked objects, configured via the `configure snmpv3 add ...` command family (see `cli-reference.md` for exact syntax):

1. **User** (`configure snmpv3 add user`) — a USM identity with its own auth (MD5/SHA) and privacy (DES/3DES/AES) credentials.
2. **Group** (`configure snmpv3 add group`) — associates one or more users with a named group under a security model (`usm`).
3. **MIB view** (`configure snmpv3 add mib-view`) — defines a named, arbitrarily precise **OID-subtree allow/deny list**: `configure snmpv3 add mib-view myView subtree <oid> {subtree-mask} type {included | excluded}`, repeatable to build up inclusion/exclusion rules against specific subtrees (e.g. grant access to `1.3.6.1.2.1.2` (`ifTable`) while excluding a narrower subtree within it). This is the mechanism's distinctive piece — rather than a single blanket read-write/read-only toggle per community/user (the v1/v2c community model), EXOS lets an admin scope exactly which OID subtrees a given group can touch.
4. **Access** (`configure snmpv3 add access`) — the object that actually ties it together: given a group name, a security level (`noauth`/`auth`/`priv`), and a security model, it assigns a **read-view**, **write-view**, and **notify-view** (each referencing a named MIB view from step 3). This is where "can this group SET objects under this subtree, at this auth/privacy level" is ultimately decided.

**Practical implication for SignalScope**: an SNMPv3 SET failing on EXOS is not just a credentials problem — it can equally be a **view-access-scope** problem (the user's group has a `write-view` that excludes the specific OID being targeted, even with fully correct auth/priv credentials). SignalScope's SNMP-write error handling for EXOS devices should surface this distinction (auth failure vs. view-access-denied, both of which SNMPv3 typically reports as a form of `authorizationError`/`noAccess` in the response PDU) rather than presenting a generic "SNMP SET failed" message — the fix in the view-access case is a `configure snmpv3 add mib-view`/`add access` change on the device, not a credential re-entry.

**Cross-reference note (per assignment brief)**: this is conceptually the same three/four-layer shape (user → group → view/policy → enforced access) as Huawei's SNMPv3 MIB-view access control documented in the Huawei vendor folder — worth normalizing into a shared concept ("SNMPv3 view-based access control", the IETF `SNMP-VIEW-BASED-ACM-MIB`/VACM standard both vendors are implementing, just with vendor-specific CLI verbs on top) in the cross-vendor comparison matrix rather than treating each vendor's version as bespoke.
